what_it_does.text: Agentforce is Salesforce's platform of autonomous AI agents, built into the Salesforce Platform, that answer questions, resolve cases, qualify leads and take actions for customers and employees around the clock. Agents are built from subagents (topics), natural-language instructions and actions made from existing Flows, prompt templates, Apex and APIs, grounded in CRM and Data 360 data, with MuleSoft, MCP and A2A reaching other systems. The Einstein Trust Layer wraps them with dynamic grounding, data masking, zero data retention, toxicity detection and an audit trail.

agents.name: Service Agent
agents.what: Customer-facing autonomous agent that replaces scripted chatbots: answers questions, resolves cases, manages orders and troubleshoots on the web, by phone and in apps, and hands off to a human with the context of the conversation.
actions: Case management, reservation management, order inquiries, account management, delivery issues and FAQs (pre-built topics and actions)
Resolve open case, draft follow-up email, escalate to specialist, pull customer history, log interaction notes
Self-service order cancellations, exchanges and returns within guardrails the business sets
Schedule field service appointments
Channels: voice, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, websites

agents.name: Employee Agent
agents.what: Agentforce for employees (formerly Einstein Copilot): works in the Salesforce org, the mobile app and Slack, searching data, summarizing accounts and opportunities, forecasting and executing action plans. The research on SalesBleed describes its General CRM subagent reading leads and accounts with a Query Records tool, and Slack subagents that search and post messages.
actions: Search data sources; summarize accounts and opportunities; forecast revenue
Query Records tool over CRM tables such as Leads and Accounts (General CRM subagent, as described by Zenity Labs)
Slack actions: Search Slack, Send a Slack Direct Message, Reply to a Slack Thread
Deployed in the Salesforce org, Salesforce mobile app and Slack

agents.name: SDR / Engagement agent
agents.what: Engages inbound leads around the clock: answers product and pricing questions, handles objections and books meetings for sellers, using CRM and external data, then routes the lead to a rep.
actions: Send a personalized introductory email to a lead
Respond to pricing questions
Access an account executive's calendar to schedule a follow-up call
Qualify, score and route leads; reminders and next-step outreach by email, chat or messaging

agents.name: Agentforce Sales agents
agents.what: Out-of-the-box sales agents announced in March 2026: prospecting, account research and meeting prep, pipeline management that updates CRM fields, and a quoting agent that generates and updates quotes within the seller's permissions; Salesforce says sellers have final approval over every agent action.
actions: Prospect and rank leads from an ideal customer profile
Generate account briefs
Update opportunity fields and recommend next steps
Generate and update quotes within governed workflows
Work in Sales Cloud, Slack, ChatGPT and Teams

agents.name: Merchandiser
agents.what: Commerce agent that helps ecommerce merchandisers with site setup, goal setting, personalized promotions, product descriptions and data-driven insights.
actions: Create personalized promotions
Write product descriptions
Site setup and data-driven insights

use_cases.name: SalesBleed: a poisoned web lead hijacks the agent (2026)
use_cases.who: Any organization running Agentforce with a public Web-to-Lead form and an agent with the default General CRM subagent (and, for the phishing variant, Slack actions). Disclosed by Zenity Labs in September 2026; Salesforce said it had no evidence the issue was exploited against any customer.

reach.what: The Leads table, which anyone on the internet can write to through the unauthenticated Web-to-Lead form; the agent reads it when an employee asks about leads
The Accounts table (company names, deal sizes), readable by the same Query Records tool because the default General CRM subagent holds read access to both Leads and Accounts
Trusted URLs, the redaction layer that strips untrusted URLs from agent output after the agent generates it
The chat surface and Slack, which fetch external image URLs and unfurl links automatically, without a click
Slack threads and channels, through the Reply to a Slack Thread action, posting under the agent's identity

mandate.what: As reported: the employee asks the agent to check the latest leads and help with the newest one

Illustrative: read the leads and accounts the employee is working on; post to Slack only with the employee's confirmation and under their name; send nothing to destinations the organization has not trusted

gap.what: One subagent identity held attacker-writable input (leads), read access to sensitive data (accounts) and an output that renders links and images: the researchers call it a version of the lethal trifecta, and say these are defaults, not misconfigurations.
The only barrier between the agent's output and the outside was redaction applied after generation, and the redactor and the renderer disagreed on what a URL is.
Reply to a Slack Thread posted without user confirmation and without naming the user who invoked it, so the agent could speak in Slack beyond what the employee asked.

controls.what: Trusted URLs enforcement for Agentforce and Einstein AI (from 8 September 2025, after ForcedLeak): an allowlist meant to stop agent output reaching untrusted URLs
Trusted URLs redaction hardened against the reported bypass (fix confirmed by Zenity Labs on 19 August 2026)

Reply to a Slack Thread now attributes the invoking user (20 August 2026) and requires user confirmation by default (21 September 2026); Salesforce says it is helping customers review their configurations
Agent access to records and fields is permissions-based and can be set per agent type and action; Trust Layer event log monitoring
Audit Trail to track AI agent actions and outputs

simulation.action: An outside attacker submits a lead through the organization's public Web-to-Lead form with hidden instructions in one of its fields
simulation.note: Web-to-Lead works as designed here. RiskMandate's record shows the Leads table as writable by anyone, so part of what the agent reads is attacker-controlled.

simulation.action: An employee asks the agent something routine: check my latest leads and help me with the newest one
Reads the poisoned lead with its Query Records tool and takes the embedded text as instructions
Queries the Accounts table with the same tool and pulls company names and deal sizes the employee never asked for
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows Accounts inside the reach of the subagent that also reads public leads, with no step between the injected instruction and the query.

simulation.action: Writes the values into a hostname and prints it back as an image tag; the crafted URL passes the Trusted URLs redaction
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the redaction layer as the only control on this path, applied after the agent had produced the output.

simulation.action: The chat surface (or Slack's link preview) fetches the URL; the DNS lookup carries the account data to the attacker's server with no click. Agentforce reported the content as blocked after the data had already left
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows an outbound path to any host from the rendering surface, and that the agent's own report of a block was not evidence of containment.

simulation.action: Following the same lead, posts a phishing link into Slack threads with Reply to a Slack Thread: no confirmation asked, no user named
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows a write action to the whole workplace with neither confirmation nor attribution in evidence, so the message's origin could not be traced to a person.

simulation.action: Zenity Labs reports on 1 June 2026; Salesforce hardens Trusted URLs, adds attribution and default confirmation, and says it has no evidence of exploitation

use_cases.name: Service Agent resolving cases, orders and refunds
use_cases.who: Customer service teams deploying the customer-facing Service Agent on their website, phone line or messaging apps (illustrated in Salesforce's training with a fictional apparel retailer whose agent recommends products, refunds orders and offers promotions).

reach.what: Cases, customer history and interaction notes
Orders: order inquiries, cancellations, exchanges, returns and refunds
Customers directly, on voice, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and websites
Unified customer profiles in Data 360, including external data connected by Zero Copy (for example loyalty data held in Databricks)
Flows, Apex, prompt templates and MuleSoft APIs turned into actions that can reach other systems

mandate.what: Illustrative: answer questions and resolve cases for the customer in the conversation, using that customer's records only
Illustrative: cancellations, returns and refunds within the published returns policy; anything outside it goes to a human with a summary

gap.what: Every Flow, Apex class or MuleSoft API made into an action extends the agent's reach to whatever that automation can touch, which can be wider than the service job.
Refunds and order changes have money consequences, and the policy check depends on data quality: Salesforce's own example shows a 30-day returns rule failing on dates in the wrong format.

controls.what: Subagent (topic) instructions act as guardrails; record and field access is permissions-based per agent type and action; Agent Preview and Testing Center
Agentforce Guardrails: user-defined safeguards plus Salesforce-managed protections that block off-topic conversations
Einstein Trust Layer: dynamic grounding, secure data retrieval within permissions, data masking, zero data retention, toxicity detection
Hand-off to human reps with the full context of the interaction

simulation.action: A customer opens the chat on the website and asks about a recent order
Looks up the customer's unified profile and order history (illustrative)
Checks the order against the 30-day returns rule; the order date arrived in another format and the check does not compute (illustrative, after Salesforce's training example)
Processes the refund anyway through a Flow action (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the refund action reachable without a human step, with the policy enforced only by data the agent could not read correctly.

simulation.action: Offers an exclusive promotion based on loyalty data from an external system (illustrative)
Calls a MuleSoft API action that also updates the customer's record in the ERP (illustrative)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows a system outside the service mandate inside the agent's reach through a reused action.

simulation.action: Hands the conversation to a human rep with a summary

use_cases.name: Banking agent disputing charges and issuing credits
use_cases.who: A bank deploying a service agent for card disputes, the example Salesforce gave at Agentforce's general availability.

reach.what: Recent transactions on the customer's account
The customer, in a conversation to identify unauthorized charges
Triggers without a person: changes in data, business rules, automations or API calls from other systems

mandate.what: Illustrative: identify disputed charges with the authenticated cardholder and open a dispute
Illustrative: provisional credits and merchant notices above a set amount wait for a human

gap.what: Salesforce describes the agent issuing provisional credits and notifying merchants all before a human needs to intervene: money and outside parties are in reach on the agent's own judgement.
Agents can start from data changes or API calls, so a dispute flow can run with no customer or employee in the loop.

controls.what: Audit Trail to track agent actions and outputs; trust patterns including design decisions for human oversight
Permissions-based access to records and fields per agent type and action
Industry compliance features extend the Trust Layer for regulated environments

simulation.action: A cardholder messages the bank about charges they do not recognize
Retrieves recent transactions from the account
Works through the list with the customer and marks three charges as unauthorized
Notifies the merchants of the disputed charges
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows outside parties contacted by the agent before any human review.

simulation.action: Issues provisional credits to the customer's account (illustrative amount above the bank's threshold)
simulation.note: RiskMandate's record shows the credit action within the agent's reach with no approval step in evidence, and prices the exposure as the credits the agent can issue.

simulation.action: A human agent picks up the case with the full context

incidents.what: ForcedLeak (CVSS 9.4, scored by the researchers): Noma Labs showed that instructions hidden in a Web-to-Lead description field could make Agentforce query CRM lead data and send it in an image request to a Salesforce-allowlisted domain that had expired and been bought for $5. Salesforce re-secured the domain, enforced Trusted URLs for Agentforce and Einstein AI from 8 September 2025, and said it had released patches that prevent output in Agentforce agents from being sent to untrusted URLs.

SalesBleed: Zenity Labs reported three flaws: two bypasses of the Trusted URLs redaction allowing zero-click exfiltration of account data from a poisoned web lead (in chat and through Slack link previews), and a Reply to a Slack Thread action that posted without confirmation or attribution, usable for phishing under the agent's identity. Salesforce fixed all three (confirmed 21 September 2026), said it had no evidence of exploitation, and changed Slack action defaults to require confirmation.

questions: The default General CRM subagent reads both Leads, which anyone can write through Web-to-Lead, and Accounts: can an admin split those so an agent reading public leads cannot query accounts, and will that become the default?
User confirmation on Slack write actions is now on by default but can be switched off with one click: is turning it off recorded in the Audit Trail, and can it be alerted on?

Trusted URLs redaction runs after the agent writes its output: is it now applied identically on every surface that renders agent output (chat, Slack, mobile, Experience sites), and can customers see a log of what was redacted?
For actions that move money, such as refunds, quotes or provisional credits, what approval thresholds can a customer set, and is each approval recorded against a named person?
Which identity does a customer-facing Service Agent run as, and can a customer list every record and system an agent can reach through its actions before it goes live?
